page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.2-32 is a flexible virtual compute instance configured with an x86_64 architecture. Compute capacity is driven by an AMD EPYC 7742 processor operating at a nominal clock speed of 2.25 GHz. The allocation provides 2 physical cores operating 2 threads per core, yielding 4 dedicated virtual CPUs. Dedicated thread allocation prevents hypervisor-level CPU contention, ensuring stable performance across computational threads.

Memory capacity is a core characteristic of this configuration, offering 32.0 GB of RAM, which equates to an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. This generous memory-to-core balance categorizes the instance within memory-optimized usage patterns. The server profile excludes discrete GPU accelerators and includes no local NVMe storage. Consequently, persistence and high-throughput disk operations require external block storage volumes, which introduces dependency on network-attached storage latency. Networking provisions include one complimentary public IPv4 address for external access.

From an efficiency perspective, the VM.Standard.E3.Flex.2-32 offers strong resource density for tasks where memory capacity requirements outpace CPU utilization. Users avoid over-provisioning compute resources merely to satisfy baseline working-set memory constraints. The system configuration is well adapted for memory-intensive workloads including Redis or Memcached caching nodes, intermediate relational database servers, extract-transform-load (ETL) data pipelines, and application backends with sizable in-memory data structures.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.2-32 is a memory-oriented virtual machine instance featuring an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. It is powered by a 2.25 GHz AMD EPYC 7742 processor built on the x86_64 architecture, configured with 2 physical cores and 4 dedicated vCPUs via simultaneous multithreading. The instance is allocated 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include dedicated hardware accelerators, featuring zero GPUs, nor does it contain bundled local storage, requiring workloads to rely entirely on external network-attached block storage for persistence. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because the hardware footprint emphasizes memory allocation over raw thread count, the instance delivers cost-effective resource density for memory-bound tasks without requiring excess compute spend. VM.Standard.E3.Flex.2-32 is appropriate for in-memory caching platforms, mid-tier relational database instances, memory-heavy background ETL operations, and standard web application hosting requiring significant working memory.
